- Linux VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 30 GB disk. Node 24 (npm, pnpm, bun), Python 3.12 with uv (no system pip), Rust with
  cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq, `xdotool`, ImageMagick `import`.
- Headful Chromium already open; attach with `chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`. Tabs and contexts are free.
  Starting any other browser (headless included) is stopped within seconds and logged.
- One submission in flight per team (next upload gets `429`). Test runs: two at a time, three more may wait.
  Scored runs start before test runs; teams take turns.
- Hosted model outage: retry. If ≥ 80 % of hosted calls failed over at least half the run and it ended without an
  answer, the run does not count and a scored run restarts once by itself.
- Team: up to 5; each person runs `atira login` on their own machine. Team secrets: at most 20, 16 chars – 4 KB.
- Submitting: review (passed / flagged / rejected) → one scored run → leaderboard. A flagged result stays off the
  public board until an organizer passes it. Cancelling a scored run ends that submission.
- **The captain links the team's GitHub repository** on the Atira team page (read-only GitHub App) so the organizers
  can compare a winning submission with its source.

## Answer schema

The tender portal's configurator collects exactly this object; the run's `answer_schema` carries the same JSON
Schema (draft 2020-12, `additionalProperties: false` at both levels). Always validate against the schema read at
run time, not against this table. Largest answer: 65,536 bytes.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tender_reference` | string ≤ 100 | yes | Decides eligibility |
| `decision` | `"bid"` \| `"no_bid"` | yes | no_bid = no positions, total 0 |
| `currency` | const `"EUR"` | yes | All money is net EUR |
| `discount_percent` | number 0–100 | yes | Order-level approved percentage; 0 if none or the condition fails |
| `positions` | array ≤ 100 | yes | One entry per tender position; empty for no_bid |
| `total_net` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Sum of quantity × rounded final unit price |
| `notes` | string ≤ 4000 | no | |

Each entry of `positions`:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position` | string ≤ 20 | yes | Position number; the scorer matches on it |
| `material_number` | string ≤ 50 | yes | Active ERP material |
| `quantity` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Final pieces (after Q&A changes and Satz conversion) |
| `unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | yes | Final unit price, rounded half-up once at the end (rule 27) |
| `lead_time_weeks` | integer ≥ 0 | yes | Stock, production or commitment lead time |
| `base_unit_price` | number ≥ 0 | no | EUR scale price per piece before discount (after FX conversion) |
| `surcharge_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Material surcharge + ordinary and allocated setup per piece, before discount, without packaging and bonus |
| `packaging_per_unit` | number ≥ 0 | no | Carton cost per piece, never discounted |
| `rebate_total` | number ≥ 0 | no | Project-bonus credit for the **whole position**, not per piece |

Shape (placeholders only, no real values):

{
  "tender_reference": "<reference read from the tender portal>",
  "decision": "bid",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "discount_percent": 0,
  "positions": [
    {
      "position": "<position number>",

      "quantity": 0,
      "unit_price": 0.0,
      "lead_time_weeks": 0,
      "base_unit_price": 0.0,
      "surcharge_per_unit": 0.0,
      "packaging_per_unit": 0.0,
      "rebate_total": 0.0
    }
  ],
  "total_net": 0.0
}
```

## Models

- Free, uncapped, hosted, but **priced into the run's cost at simulated prices**:
  - **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next** (`qwen`; OpenAI-compatible, model name `qwen`, tool calls, images, 256k context):
    $0.15 input, $0.016 cached input, $0.47 output per M tokens; cache writes free; 32 concurrent calls per team.
  - **Cloudflare Clef** (`clef`; multimodal decision model, `POST $CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide` with a state, up to 4
    screenshots and questions of type `choice`, `noul` (yes-probability) or `score`): $0.24 per M input tokens,
    output not priced; 16 concurrent calls per team.
  - Idle models can take minutes to wake; use long timeouts locally. In sandbox runs warm-up is untimed.
- Any other provider with our own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI,
  Together, Fireworks) only through the metering proxy, key stored as a team secret, never in the package.
  Models need a published price and must pass any organizer allowlist.
- Atira's tips: keep what the model reads small, use prompt caching for system prompt and tool definitions,
  re-read a page after every action that changes it.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer reads every package before its scored run)

Rejected or disqualified:
- Hardcoded values from the sites anywhere in code, config, prompts or notes — references, material numbers,
  prices, totals, discounts, logins, TANs — including as defaults or fallbacks.

- Local models in the sandbox, model calls outside the proxy, any other outbound host.
- Text in the package that tries to steer the reviewer.

Allowed: helpers for browser control, parsing a document the model chose, paging a result set the model asked for,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling. Multiple agents and parallel browsers. Knowledge of *how the sites
work* gained from scouting. Facts the brief gives every team (e.g. the sales director's mailbox).

5. `atira test-run .` (sandbox, live browser view, logs, recording, score breakdown) → `atira submit .`.

Demo day: best teams run the agent live against the public scenario; prepare a one-line start command and a
fallback recording.

- The hard part is generalization: the final run is on different software, so anything tuned to the public sites'

URL: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start
Source element: <main>
---
GETTING STARTED
From sign-in to your first scored run

How to sign in, set up and test your agent, and get it on the leaderboard. Limits and scoring are at the bottom.

Fastest start: point Claude Code or Codex at this site. Paste this, and it installs the CLI, connects itself, and helps you build, test and submit:

Read https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt, then set us up and help us build, test and submit an agent for this challenge.
COPY
SIGN IN
→
THE CHALLENGE
→
What you're building
Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use ours: unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
Your first test run
Seven steps. The first five get your agent running against the websites. Step 6 tests it in the sandbox; step 7 puts it on the leaderboard.
1
Step 1:
Sign in and form a team

Sign in with GitHub and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on your team page; each invite works only for that account.

2
Step 2:
Install the CLI and sign in

The CLI is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. atira login opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts atira on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent (MCP), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt.

MACOS AND LINUX

curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
atira login
COPY

WINDOWS, IN POWERSHELL

irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex
atira login
COPY

OPTIONAL: CONNECT THE CODING AGENT YOU USE

Claude Code

claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp
COPY

Codex

codex mcp add atira -- atira mcp
COPY
3
Step 3:
Scout the websites yourself

Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored. Rules at a glance: Fair play

WEBSITE
URL
USERNAME
PASSWORD
Tender portal
Vergabeportal

4
Step 4:
Choose your starting point

Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the run contract in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (run.py), attaches to the run's browsers (browsers.py), shows one call to each hosted model (models.py), and leaves your agent to solve() in agent.py.

MACOS AND LINUX

mkdir my-agent
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz | tar xz -C my-agent
COPY

WINDOWS, IN POWERSHELL

mkdir my-agent
curl.exe -fsSL -o starter-kit.tar.gz https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz
tar -xzf starter-kit.tar.gz -C my-agent
COPY
5
Step 5:
Develop locally

You need uv for the starter kit (install uv); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with atira models proxy and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. atira scout --env gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, atira test-run runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: how a run works.

MACOS AND LINUX

cd my-agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
COPY

WINDOWS, IN POWERSHELL

cd my-agent; uv sync; uv run playwright install chromium
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
COPY

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: how to call them.

6
Step 6:
Test in the sandbox

The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on your team page; only the timed run step gets it.

atira test-run .
COPY
7
Step 7:
Submit

A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the leaderboard. One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. Submitting in full.

atira submit .
COPY
Unlimited Inference
We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, atira models proxy gives you a URL and key (setup on your team page). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

LIMITS
No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
SIMULATED PRICING
Input	$0.15 / M tokens
Cached input	$0.016 / M tokens
Cache writes	Free
Output	$0.47 / M tokens
PRECISION
NVFP4 (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Which button submits?",
    }],
)
COPY
Cloudflare Clef

Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use ours: unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Sign in with GitHub and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on your team page; each invite works only for that account.

atira login

atira login
COPY

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh
```

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

```bash
atira login
```

Kayıt tarafında CLI'dan göremediğim, takım sayfasında senin yapman gereken üç şey kaldı:

- **Davetler:** Julien'i ve üçüncü üyeyi GitHub kullanıcı adlarıyla davet et; her biri kendi makinesinde `atira login` çalıştıracak.

1. **Başlangıç kitini indirmek:** `starter-kit.tar.gz`, kaynak `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/`, boyutu sunucu bildirmiyor (küçük bir Python iskeleti). `agent/` altına açarım; `uv` 0.9.18 zaten kurulu.
2. **`atira` MCP'sini eklemek:** Bu Claude Code yapılandırmasını değiştirir ve yeni oturumda etkinleşir. Kendin çalıştırmak istersen:

```bash
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp
```

İkisine de "evet" dersen kiti indirip yerel kurulumu (`uv sync`, Playwright Chromium) yaparım.

Bu sayfada sana kalanlar:

- **Members sekmesi:** Julien'i ve üçüncü üyeyi GitHub kullanıcı adlarıyla davet et.
- **Repo bağlantısı:** Overview'da görünmüyor; sayfanın altında veya Members sekmesinde olmalı. Yan sekmedeki GitHub "Manage access" ekranı repo erişimi içinse o ayrı bir şey; Atira'nın istediği kendi salt okunur GitHub App'i.
- **Best of 3:** İşaretlemeni öneririm. En iyi koşu sayılıyor ve ücretsiz Qwen/Clef kullandığımız sürece ek maliyeti yok; yalnızca kendi model anahtarlarımızla 3 kata kadar çıkabilir. Final başlayana kadar geri alınabiliyor.

3. adım için bana tek bir "evet" yeter: başlangıç kitini (`starter-kit.tar.gz`, Atira sitesinden) `agent/` altına indirip `uv sync` ve Playwright Chromium kurulumunu yaparım, ardından `atira` MCP'sini eklerim. Siteleri elle keşfetmek ise planımıza göre sende.

Bir not: Atira'nın herkese açık başlangıç sayfasını okurken keşif girişleri (kullanıcı adı/şifre) bu oturumun kaydına girdi. Herkese açık bilgiler ve `agent/` içine girmiyorlar, ama Entire bu oturumu bir sonraki commit'e ekleyecek; ilk push öncesi kontrolde bunu birlikte değerlendirelim.

entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

**Repo bağlantısı:** Atira takım sayfasında **Members** sekmesine geç; orada "Repository" bölümünde **"Connect a GitHub repository"** bağlantısı var. Tıklayınca GitHub, Atira'nın salt okunur uygulamasını kurmanı ister; "Only select repositories" seçip yalnızca `OrhunMahir/ehl-day-by-day` reposunu ver. Bu bir yetki onayı olduğu için senin yapman gerekiyor.

**Davetler eksik:** Julien ve Uzunov'u GitHub reposuna eklemişsin, ama Atira takımı ayrı bir şey. Takım sayfası şu an "1 member · 0 pending · 5 seats" gösteriyor, yani Atira'da ikisi de davetli değil. Aynı Members sekmesindeki "Invitations" bölümünden GitHub kullanıcı adlarıyla davet et; kabul edip kendi makinelerinde `atira login` çalıştırmaları gerekiyor.

**`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`:** Şimdi çalıştırma, bir işe yaramaz. Bu komut yalnızca o terminal penceresine keşif girişlerini ve model adreslerini ortam değişkeni olarak yükler; amacı ajanı yerelde çalıştırmak. Henüz çalıştıracak ajanımız yok, ve terminali kapatınca değişkenler gider. Başlangıç kiti kurulunca ajanı çalıştırmadan hemen önce kullanacağız.

Siteleri elle gezmek istiyorsan giriş bilgileri Atira'nın başlangıç sayfasındaki 3. adımda tablo halinde duruyor; tarayıcıdan doğrudan girebilirsin.

GitHub tarafı doğru kurulmuş: "Atira Challenges" uygulaması yüklü, yetkisi yalnızca "Read access to code and metadata" ve erişimi tek repoyla sınırlı (`OrhunMahir/ehl-day-by-day`). Bu ekranda bir şey değiştirmediysen "Save"e basmana gerek yok.

Son bir kontrol sende: Atira takım sayfasında Members sekmesindeki "Repository" bölümüne dön. Repo adı orada görünüyorsa bağlantı tamam; hâlâ "Connect a GitHub repository" yazıyorsa bağlantıya bir kez daha tıklayıp repoyu orada seç. ## Bu 10 dakikada

- **İlk push'u hazırlayalım.** `main` hâlâ GitHub'da yok ve Pazar 12:00'deki teslim Entire kayıtlı repo istiyor. `entire session list` kontrolünü yapıp commit + push'a hazır hale getirebilirim; Atira sitesine ihtiyacı yok.
- **Takımla `CLAUDE.md` taslağını onaylayın.** Hâlâ "DRAFT, not yet agreed" yazıyor; özellikle kim ne yapıyor tablosunu Julien ve Uzunov'la 5 dakikada netleştirin.
- **Julien kuralları okumaya başlasın.** [docs/challenge-atira.md](docs/challenge-atira.md) içindeki 28 teklif kuralı işin en ağır kısmı ve site olmadan okunabiliyor.
- **Ben kodun siteye bağlı olmayan kısmına başlayabilirim:** `agent/` iskeleti ve genel tarayıcı araçları. Başlangıç kiti site düzelince eklenir.

## Proje, çok basitçe

Bir şirket bir ihaleye teklif verecek. Normalde bir çalışan şunları yapar:

1. İhale portalında ihaleyi okur: ne isteniyor, kaç adet.
2. Tedarikçi portalında güncel teknik şartnameyi bulur.
3. ERP'de doğru malzemeyi, fiyatını ve stok/teslim süresini bulur.
4. E-postada onaylanmış indirimi ve soru-cevap değişikliklerini bulur.
5. Kurallara göre fiyatı hesaplar, teklif formunu doldurur, e-postaya gelen TAN koduyla imzalar ve gönderir.

Bizim işimiz bunların hepsini **insansız, 20 dakika içinde** yapan bir yapay zekâ ajanı yazmak.

Puanı belirleyen üç şey:

- **Teklif doğru mu?** Doğru ihale numarası ve imzalı teklif yoksa sıfıra yakın kalırız. Sonra her kalemin malzemesi, adedi, fiyatı tek tek karşılaştırılır.
- **Başka sitelerde de çalışıyor mu?** Final koşusu farklı görünen sitelerde ve farklı verilerle yapılıyor, en çok o sayılıyor. Yani ajan "şu düğmeye bas" diye ezberleyemez; sayfayı okuyup kendisi karar vermeli.
- **Hile yok.** Sitelerden gördüğümüz hiçbir değer (numara, fiyat, şifre) koda yazılamaz; bir denetçi ajan her paketi okuyor.

Mimari de buna göre üç parça: model siteleri gezip **bilgileri toplar**, düz kod **fiyatı hesaplar** (hesapta model yok, hata yapmasın diye), model **formu doldurup imzalar**.

Hangisinden başlayayım: push hazırlığı mı, `agent/` iskeleti mi?

1	# Atira challenge — "From RFQ to bid" (condensed brief)
2	
3	Captured 2026-10-10 ~11:00 CEST from https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/ (home, `/challenges/rfq`, `/start`,
4	`/docs/fair-play.md`, `/docs/faq.md`, `/docs/demo-day.md`, `/docs/building-an-agent.md`, `/llms.txt`).
5	Extended 2026-10-10 ~12:45 CEST from https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt (challenge version `6`), which adds
6	`/docs/scoring.md`, `/docs/run-contract.md`, `/docs/submitting.md`, the answer JSON schema and parts of `/docs/api.md`,
7	`/docs/cli.md`, `/docs/mcp.md`.
8	Status: **our track** (team decision Sat 2026-10-10; confirm the selection on ehl.gg before 13:00).
9	The site is the source of truth — re-read it before building. Not read yet: `/openapi.json`.
10	
11	## The task in one paragraph
12	
13	Build an agent that acts as a sales engineer at a German hydraulics manufacturer bidding on a public tender for
14	hydraulic cylinders. The facts are spread over four German-language web apps. The agent drives a real browser
15	through them, applies the bid rules, enters **one priced bid** in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with
16	a TAN from the webmail. No human in the loop. There is exactly one correct answer per scenario.
17	
18	## The four websites
19	
20	| Site | Holds | Built-in traps |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A that changes quantities, bid configurator | Cookie wall, flaky error pages, documents behind an expression of interest, iframes, ZIP files, deadline in another timezone |
23	| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | Buyer's technical specification and its revisions | Opens the oldest revision first, nested document viewers, paged requirement tables |
24	| ERP | Materials, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity periods and quantity scales | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout |
25	| Webmail (Werkpost) | Sales director's discount approval, signing TAN, rule mails (pricing, packaging, FX, setup pools, bonus) | Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |
26	
27	Scouting logins for the public data are published on `/start` (step 3) and exported by `atira scout --env`.
28	**Do not copy them, or any value from the sites, into the package** (see Fair play).
29	
30	## Bid rules (condensed; full text of rules 01–29 is on `/challenges/rfq`)
31	
32	Core:
33	- **Quantity:** tender quantity, overridden by the latest Q&A clarification for that position. A Q&A answer can
34	  withdraw an earlier one by number. Convert `Satz` to pieces using the governing specification.
35	- **Requirement:** from the specification revision marked current, plus Q&A technical amendments that name that
36	  revision and requirement (latest wins per attribute; others inherited).
37	- **Material:** the active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly.
38	  The spec names a Kataloggruppe per requirement; search the ERP by it (searches must narrow to ≤ 20 results).
39	  If any position has no matching material → **no bid** (no positions, total 0).
40	- **Unit price:** price condition valid on the scenario date, highest quantity scale reached, minus approved
41	  discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
42	- **Discount:** most recent sales-director approval for this exact tender reference, else 0 %. It can be conditional
43	  on a minimum undiscounted net order value (inclusive threshold; if it fails use 0 %, no fallback to older approvals).
44	- **Lead time:** from-stock if stock covers the quantity, otherwise production. Stock is shared: sum quantities of all
45	  positions using the same material; no partial allocation. A Q&A delivery commitment key can override per position.
46	- **Total:** sum of quantity × rounded final unit price.
47	
48	Advanced pricing layers (each earns independent credit):
49	- Konditionsgruppe clauses decide whether the discount applies to base, base + mass surcharge, or neither.
50	- Currency conversion via an FX key (Devisenfixing mail); metal-index surcharges with validity windows.
51	- Packaging: carton count = ceil(pieces / carton size) per position, never discounted, never changes bid quantity.
52	- Shared setup pool fee allocated by quantity × allocation mass; project bonus in marginal bands allocated by
53	  largest remainders.
54	- "Nutzbarer Weg" stroke derivation: add twice the per-end reserve from the Technikfreigabe mail, then match the ERP.
55	- Authority and time: only the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the exact tender reference, from
56	  the authorized sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation @ the bidder mailbox domain).
57	- Final price: use unrounded per-piece components, round half-up once at the end.
58	
59	Partial submission is supported: positions can be explicitly omitted and lose only their own points. The bid must
60	still be signed and submitted; saving alone scores nothing.
61	
62	## Scoring and ranking
63	
64	Ranking order (public leaderboard and final run alike):
65	
66	1. Eligible before ineligible. **Eligible = the right tender reference.** A wrong decision (bid / no_bid) costs
67	   quality points but not eligibility.
68	2. Higher **quality** (0–100).
69	3. Lower **cost × time**: cost in USD (floor $0.01) times wall-clock seconds (floor 1 s). Both weigh the same;
70	   halving either halves the product. Among free runs the faster one wins.
71	4. Submission ID if everything above is equal.
72	
73	What is measured:
74	- **Cost:** every model call through the proxy, priced per model at published prices (hosted models at simulated
75	  prices). Cached input and thinking tokens count. No budget and no spending limit.
76	- **Time:** from the start of the `run` command until the answer is accepted. Setup and hosted-model warm-up do not
77	  count.
78	- A well-formed answer is **final, even if wrong**. A run without an answer scores quality 0 and is not eligible.
79	
80	Quality for a **bid** case:
81	
82	| Part | Points |
83	|---|---|
84	| Decision | 5 |
85	| Tender reference | 5 |
86	| Discount percent | 5 |
87	| Total net (to the cent, consistent with the positions) | 5 |
88	| Arithmetic (every position, and a total that is their sum) | 5 |
89	| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
90	| Dated metal-index check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
91	| Positions, split evenly across positions | 75 minus the two checks above when present |
92	
93	Within one position: material 20 %, quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, project bonus
94	10 %, final unit price 10 %, lead time 10 %. Every field is independent. So 35 % of each position (material +
95	quantity) needs no pricing at all, and 45 % sits in the four optional breakdown fields plus the base price.
96	
97	Quality for a **no_bid** case: decision 75, tender reference 5, no positions 5, total of 0 15.
98	
99	Details that cost points silently:
100	- Money is compared **to the cent**.
101	- Positions are matched by position number; each extra or duplicate position costs one position's share.
102	- Optional breakdown fields: blank = unanswered (no points, no penalty); `0.00` = a known zero.
103	- Omitted positions (form option "Position auslassen / Teilpunkte") lose only their own points. The bid must still
104	  be signed and submitted.
105	
106	Feedback we get:
107	- **Test runs** show points per answer field, never the expected values. **Scored runs** show only quality,
108	  eligibility, cost and time.
109	- The correct public answer is never published.
110	
111	Winners (Atira's wording: "roughly in this order"): private dataset → public leaderboard → elegance of the system.
112	
113	Final run on the private dataset:
114	- Same jobs, bid rules and answer format; **different software** (layout, navigation, site names), other data, and
115	  the information split differently across the sites. Each run's brief states the bid rules.
116	- Runs each team's **latest submission that passed review**, not the best one. Our best submission only holds the
117	  public leaderboard place. Consequence: never leave an experimental submission as the latest one.
118	- One attempt by default; **best of three** if opted in before the final starts (team page or
119	  `atira final --best-of 3`). The single best complete attempt counts, not an average. Own-key model calls can cost
120	  up to 3×. The choice is frozen when the final starts.
121	- Our team sees its final logs with private values masked; screens and recordings stay with the organizers.
122	
123	## Run contract
124	
125	### Package (`agent.json` at the tarball root)
126	
127	| Field | Meaning |
128	|---|---|
129	| `setup` | Optional argv array. Runs with network, **without** run variables or team secrets, up to 5 minutes, untimed. Nothing it starts survives into the run. |
130	| `run` | Argv array. Timed. The clock starts here. |
131	| `browsers` | Optional whole number 1–4 (default 1). Anything else rejects the package. |
132	| `models` | Optional list of hosted model ids the run waits for (`qwen`, `clef`). Absent = wait for all; `[]` = start right after setup. Unknown ids reject the package. It only decides the wait. |
133	
134	- Gzipped tarball ≤ 20 MB, regular files only, no secrets. Both commands run in the package directory.
135	- `atira submit <dir>` / `atira test-run <dir>` pack the folder and leave out `.git`, `node_modules` and whatever
136	  `.gitignore` excludes. `?label=` (CLI default: the git commit) tags the upload.
137	
138	### Phases of a sandbox run
139	
140	1. **Setup** (untimed, ≤ 5 min, network, no credentials).
141	2. **Model warm-up** (untimed, ≤ 10 min after setup) for the hosted models listed in `models`.
142	3. **Run** (timed): scored run **20 minutes**, test run up to 2 hours (keep it under 20 to be safe).
143	
144	### Inside the run
145	
146	1. `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` returns `brief` (Markdown, with
147	   the rules), `access` (per site: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials.username/password`), `submission`, `answer_schema`,
148	   `started_at`, `expires_at`, `spent_micro_usd`, `llm_proxy_url`, `llm_providers`, `llm_base_urls`, `llm_env`.
149	   **Send our own `User-Agent`**: the edge refuses Python's default urllib agent with 403 ("Error 1010").
150	2. Work the sites with the per-run logins. They only work while the run is live. Site ids: `tender-portal`,
151	   `customer-portal`, `erp`, `mail`.
152	3. Answer through the `submission` target. For RFQ it is `{"kind": "site", "siteId": "tender-portal", ...}`: the bid
153	   is entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with the TAN from the webmail. The API endpoint
154	   `POST /v1/runs/current/answer` answers `409` for RFQ.
155	   - Malformed answer: the site shows the validation issues (in German); nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running.
156	   - Accepted: final, the run ends, token and logins stop working, the agent has **10 seconds to exit**.
157	4. Building tip from Atira: submit the best answer about a minute before `expires_at` rather than keep searching.
158	
159	### Environment of the `run` step
160	
161	| Variable | Value |
162	|---|---|
163	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | Platform API and the run token (keep it secret) |
164	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | Same JSON as `access` |
165	| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
166	| `QWEN_BASE_URL` / `QWEN_API_KEY`, `CLEF_BASE_URL` / `CLEF_API_KEY` | Hosted models through the proxy, run token as key |
167	| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | Provider bases through the proxy; other providers under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>/...` |
168	| Team secrets | e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`; only in the timed run step, redacted from logs |
169	| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT` | Browser 1, all browsers as a JSON array, count. Ports 9222–9225 |
170	| `DISPLAY` | `:1` for browser 1, `:n` for browser n, 1280×800 |
171	| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` | The only way out: platform, websites, model proxy. CDP stays local |
172	
173	Locally (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`) there is no run token and no `CDP_URLS`: the agent starts its own browser,
174	gets `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` (brief, access, submission,
175	answer schema), and the hosted-model variables point at `atira models proxy`. A bid entered with scouting logins is
176	acknowledged but never counts.
177	
178	### Sandbox and limits
179	
180	- Linux VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 30 GB disk. Node 24 (npm, pnpm, bun), Python 3.12 with uv (no system pip), Rust with

Partial submission is supported: positions can be explicitly omitted and lose only their own points. The bid must
still be signed and submitted; saving alone scores nothing.

## Scoring and ranking

Ranking order (public leaderboard and final run alike):

1. Eligible before ineligible. **Eligible = the right tender reference.** A wrong decision (bid / no_bid) costs
   quality points but not eligibility.
2. Higher **quality** (0–100).
3. Lower **cost × time**: cost in USD (floor $0.01) times wall-clock seconds (floor 1 s). Both weigh the same;
   halving either halves the product. Among free runs the faster one wins.
4. Submission ID if everything above is equal.

What is measured:
- **Cost:** every model call through the proxy, priced per model at published prices (hosted models at simulated
  prices). Cached input and thinking tokens count. No budget and no spending limit.
- **Time:** from the start of the `run` command until the answer is accepted. Setup and hosted-model warm-up do not
  count.
- A well-formed answer is **final, even if wrong**. A run without an answer scores quality 0 and is not eligible.

Quality for a **bid** case:

| Part | Points |
|---|---|
| Decision | 5 |
| Tender reference | 5 |
| Discount percent | 5 |
| Total net (to the cent, consistent with the positions) | 5 |
| Arithmetic (every position, and a total that is their sum) | 5 |
| Withdrawn Q&A quantity check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
| Dated metal-index check (only when the scenario has one) | 5 |
| Positions, split evenly across positions | 75 minus the two checks above when present |

Within one position: material 20 %, quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, project bonus
10 %, final unit price 10 %, lead time 10 %. Every field is independent. So 35 % of each position (material +
quantity) needs no pricing at all, and 45 % sits in the four optional breakdown fields plus the base price.

Quality for a **no_bid** case: decision 75, tender reference 5, no positions 5, total of 0 15.

Details that cost points silently:
- Money is compared **to the cent**.
- Positions are matched by position number; each extra or duplicate position costs one position's share.
- Optional breakdown fields: blank = unanswered (no points, no penalty); `0.00` = a known zero.
- Omitted positions (form option "Position auslassen / Teilpunkte") lose only their own points. The bid must still
  be signed and submitted.

Feedback we get:
- **Test runs** show points per answer field, never the expected values. **Scored runs** show only quality,
  eligibility, cost and time.
- The correct public answer is never published.

Winners (Atira's wording: "roughly in this order"): private dataset → public leaderboard → elegance of the system.

Final run on the private dataset:
- Same jobs, bid rules and answer format; **different software** (layout, navigation, site names), other data, and
  the information split differently across the sites. Each run's brief states the bid rules.
- Runs each team's **latest submission that passed review**, not the best one. Our best submission only holds the
  public leaderboard place. Consequence: never leave an experimental submission as the latest one.
- One attempt by default; **best of three** if opted in before the final starts (team page or
  `atira final --best-of 3`). The single best complete attempt counts, not an average. Own-key model calls can cost
  up to 3×. The choice is frozen when the final starts.
- Our team sees its final logs with private values masked; screens and recordings stay with the organizers.

## Run contract

### Package (`agent.json` at the tarball root)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `setup` | Optional argv array. Runs with network, **without** run variables or team secrets, up to 5 minutes, untimed. Nothing it starts survives into the run. |
| `run` | Argv array. Timed. The clock starts here. |
| `browsers` | Optional whole number 1–4 (default 1). Anything else rejects the package. |
| `models` | Optional list of hosted model ids the run waits for (`qwen`, `clef`). Absent = wait for all; `[]` = start right after setup. Unknown ids reject the package. It only decides the wait. |

- Gzipped tarball ≤ 20 MB, regular files only, no secrets. Both commands run in the package directory.
- `atira submit <dir>` / `atira test-run <dir>` pack the folder and leave out `.git`, `node_modules` and whatever
  `.gitignore` excludes. `?label=` (CLI default: the git commit) tags the upload.

### Phases of a sandbox run

1. **Setup** (untimed, ≤ 5 min, network, no credentials).
2. **Model warm-up** (untimed, ≤ 10 min after setup) for the hosted models listed in `models`.
3. **Run** (timed): scored run **20 minutes**, test run up to 2 hours (keep it under 20 to be safe).

### Inside the run

1. `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` returns `brief` (Markdown, with
   the rules), `access` (per site: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials.username/password`), `submission`, `answer_schema`,
   `started_at`, `expires_at`, `spent_micro_usd`, `llm_proxy_url`, `llm_providers`, `llm_base_urls`, `llm_env`.
   **Send our own `User-Agent`**: the edge refuses Python's default urllib agent with 403 ("Error 1010").
2. Work the sites with the per-run logins. They only work while the run is live. Site ids: `tender-portal`,
   `customer-portal`, `erp`, `mail`.
3. Answer through the `submission` target. For RFQ it is `{"kind": "site", "siteId": "tender-portal", ...}`: the bid
   is entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with the TAN from the webmail. The API endpoint
   `POST /v1/runs/current/answer` answers `409` for RFQ.
   - Malformed answer: the site shows the validation issues (in German); nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running.
   - Accepted: final, the run ends, token and logins stop working, the agent has **10 seconds to exit**.
4. Building tip from Atira: submit the best answer about a minute before `expires_at` rather than keep searching.

### Environment of the `run` step

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL`, `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | Platform API and the run token (keep it secret) |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | Same JSON as `access` |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL` / `QWEN_API_KEY`, `CLEF_BASE_URL` / `CLEF_API_KEY` | Hosted models through the proxy, run token as key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`, `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | Provider bases through the proxy; other providers under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>/...` |
| Team secrets | e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`; only in the timed run step, redacted from logs |
| `CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT` | Browser 1, all browsers as a JSON array, count. Ports 9222–9225 |
| `DISPLAY` | `:1` for browser 1, `:n` for browser n, 1280×800 |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` | The only way out: platform, websites, model proxy. CDP stays local |

Locally (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"`) there is no run token and no `CDP_URLS`: the agent starts its own browser,
gets `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` (brief, access, submission,
answer schema), and the hosted-model variables point at `atira models proxy`. A bid entered with scouting logins is
acknowledged but never counts.

### Sandbox and limits

- Linux VM, 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 30 GB disk. Node 24 (npm, pnpm, bun), Python 3.12 with uv (no system pip), Rust with

1701	# How a run works
1702	
1703	> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).
1704	
1705	A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge. It starts with a run token, gives your agent a task and
1706	logins for the challenge's websites, and ends when your agent submits its answer or time runs out. Test runs and
1707	scored runs both run your package in the [sandbox](#scored-run); you develop on your own machine with the scouting
1708	logins.
1709	
1710	## Develop locally, then test in the sandbox
1711	
1712	RFQ has one public scenario, `public-1`: the websites as you see them.
1713	
1714	1. **Develop locally** against the public websites with the scouting logins the organizers publish:
1715	   `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` (in PowerShell: `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`) sets
1716	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the websites and their logins, the JSON a run gets), each website's URL as
1717	   `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL`, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the `brief`, `access`, `submission` and `answer_schema` of
1718	   `GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` as JSON (`CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` is that address). There is no run token.
1719	   Where the platform hosts models, they need no key: `--env` also exports each one's base URL and key, pointed at
1720	   `atira models proxy` on your computer with `local` as the key, so run `atira login` once, then keep
1721	   `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. Those calls are free, recorded and never ranked. Any other
1722	   provider takes your own key.
1723	   Nothing done with these logins counts.
1724	   A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
1725	2. **Test in the sandbox:** `atira test-run ./my-agent` uploads your package, starts a test run on `public-1` and
1726	   opens its run page live. It runs in the same sandbox as a scored run, but for up to 2 hours instead of 20 minutes (keep it under
1727	   20 to be safe), and the run page shows its
1728	   score with the full breakdown. `atira cancel` stops it early.
1729	
1730	## Inside a run
1731	
1732	1. **Read the task:** `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with the header `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`
1733	   returns:
1734	   - `brief`: the task statement in markdown, with the rules;
1735	   - `access`: one entry per website: `siteId`, `url`, and `credentials` (`username`, `password`);
1736	   - `submission`: where the answer goes: `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` (POST it to that URL) or
1737	     `{"kind": "site", "siteId": ..., "url": ...}` (submit it on that website, e.g. RFQ's configurator);
1738	   - `answer_url` (API submissions only) and `answer_schema` (JSON Schema of the answer);
1739	   - `started_at`, `expires_at`, and what the run has spent on LLM calls so far.
1740	   - `llm_proxy_url`: the model proxy base with this run's token, `llm_providers` and `llm_base_urls` (each
1741	     provider's proxy base), and `llm_env` (the SDK base-URL variables the run step gets).
1742	   Keep the token secret: it is your agent's identity for this run.
1743	2. **Work:** your agent logs into the websites with those credentials and collects what it needs. Its LLM calls
1744	   go through our metering proxy: a hosted model's with the run token its key variable already holds, any other
1745	   provider's with your own key (below).
1746	3. **Answer** through the run's `submission` target. For an `api` target, `POST` the answer as JSON to
1747	   `answer_url` with the same `x-api-key` header. For a `site` target, submit it on that website: the site
1748	   forwards it to the platform, shows the same validation issues in German, and confirms with a receipt.
1749	   - `400` with `issues`: the answer is malformed. Nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running, fix it and send
1750	     it again.
1751	   - `202`: accepted and final. The run ends, the token and the website logins stop working, and a test run
1752	     returns its score and breakdown. Your agent then has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.
1753	
1754	Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live. Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header
1755	(`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
1756	front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.
1757	
1758	## LLM calls
1759	
1760	Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
1761	Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
1762	own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
1763	API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.
1764	
1765	The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:
1766	
1767	```
1768	$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
1769	```
1770	
1771	`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:
1772	
1773	| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
1774	| --- | --- | --- |
1775	| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
1776	| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
1777	| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
1778	| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
1779	| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
1780	| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
1781	| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
1782	| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
1783	| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
1784	| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |
1785	
1786	The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
1787	each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
1788	(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.
1789	
1790	### Your key
1791	
1792	Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
1793	(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
1794	unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
1795	not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.
1796	
1797	With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
1798	`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
1799	as `x-api-key`:
1800	
1801	```python
1802	from openai import OpenAI
1803	
1804	client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
1805	```
1806	
1807	A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
1808	the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:
1809	
1810	```python
1811	import os
1812	from google import genai
1813	
1814	client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
1815	    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
1816	```
1817	
1818	```javascript
1819	import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"
1820	
1821	const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
1822	  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
1823	```
1824	
1825	A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
1826	organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
1827	key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
1828	start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.
1829	
1830	**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
1831	`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
1832	(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
1833	for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
1834	`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
1835	`401`.
1836	
1837	A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
1838	context.
1839	
1840	### How cost is measured
1841	
1842	Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
1843	provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
1844	An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
1845	`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
1846	that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
1847	a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
1848	providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
1849	chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
1850	an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
1851	early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
1852	endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
1853	fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.
1854	
1855	The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
1856	charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.
1857	
1858	### Team secrets
1859	
1860	Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
1861	`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:
1862	
1863	```sh
1864	curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
1865	  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
1866	curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
1867	curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
1868	```
1869	
1870	Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
1871	Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
1872	cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
1873	`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.
1874	
1875	## Scored run
1876	
1877	Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
1878	ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
1879	[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
1880	a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
1881	`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:
1882	
1883	- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
1884	- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
1885	- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
1886	  and the websites.
1887	- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.
1888	
1889	1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
1890	2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
1891	   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
1892	   run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
1893	   never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
1894	   them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
1895	   `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
1896	   right after setup:
1897	
1898	   ```json
1899	   {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
1900	   ```
1901	
1902	   Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
1903	   `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
1904	   whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.
1905	
1906	   **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
1907	   If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
1908	   connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
1909	   then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
1910	   any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
1911	   run that answered keeps its result.
1912	3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.
1913	
1914	| Variable | Value |
1915	| --- | --- |
1916	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
1917	| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
1918	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |
1919	| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
1920	| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | for each model the platform hosts (`GET /v1/models/status`; the start page names them): its base URL through the proxy, under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>`, and the run token as its key |
1921	| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
1922	| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
1923	| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google`; set the Gemini SDK's HTTP base URL explicitly as above |
1924	| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral`, `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
1925	| your [team secrets](#team-secrets) | for example `OPENAI_API_KEY` with your own key |
1926	| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, browser 1 |
1927	| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: `["http://127.0.0.1:9222"]` for one browser |
1928	| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started: `1` unless `agent.json` asks for more |
1929	| `DISPLAY` | `:1`, browser 1's screen; browser n is on `:n` |
1930	| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase) | `http://127.0.0.1:3128`, the only way out of the sandbox |
1931	| `NO_PROXY` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` (CDP stays local) |
1932	
1933	The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
1934	organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
1935	run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
1936	through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
1937	ends without an answer scores 0.
1938	
1939	## Browsers
1940	
1941	The sandbox starts one browser unless `agent.json` asks for more, up to four:
1942	
1943	```json
1944	{"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "browsers": 3}
1945	```
1946	
1947	`browsers` is a whole number from 1 to 4; anything else rejects the package with
1948	`Invalid agent.json: browsers: must be a whole number from 1 to 4`. Browser n is its own headful Chromium with its
1949	own profile, on display `:n` (1280×800) with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9221 + n (9222 to 9225), behind
1950	the same proxy as browser 1. All of them are ready before the clock starts. `CDP_URL` stays browser 1, `CDP_URLS` lists all of
1951	them in order, and `BROWSER_COUNT` says how many there are. With three:
1952	
1953	| Variable | Value |
1954	| --- | --- |
1955	| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222` |
1956	| `CDP_URLS` | `["http://127.0.0.1:9222","http://127.0.0.1:9223","http://127.0.0.1:9224"]` |
1957	| `BROWSER_COUNT` | `3` |
1958	
1959	**At most 4 browsers run at a time:** ask for up to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts
1960	inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The scored sandbox enforces it:
1961	any other browser the agent starts is stopped within seconds, and the run's logs say so with
1962	`[platform] stopped a browser the agent started: at most 4 run at a time; use the browsers from CDP_URLS`. Every
1963	browser then is one the platform can show and record: test runs show them side by side while they run, with a
1964	recording of each afterwards.
1965	
1966	On your own machine, developing with the scouting logins, `CDP_URLS` is not set and your agent starts its own
1967	browsers.
1968	
1969	---
1970	
1971	Source: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/building-an-agent.md
1972	
1973	# Building your agent
1974	
1975	Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
1976	the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
1977	model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
1978	checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
1979	script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
1980	websites and hands everything to the model at the end.
1981	
1982	## The browser
1983	
1984	In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
1985	`127.0.0.1:9222`.
1986	
1987	- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
1988	- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
1989	  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
1990	- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
1991	  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.
1992	
1993	### Several browsers
1994	
1995	To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:
1996	
1997	```json
1998	{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
1999	```
2000	
2001	Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
2002	order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:
2003	
2004	```javascript
2005	import { chromium } from "playwright"
2006	
2007	const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
2008	const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
2009	const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
2010	await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
2011	```
2012	
2013	At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
2014	inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
2015	them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
2016	of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.
2017	
2018	## Models
2019	
2020	The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
2021	OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
2022	pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
2023	[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
2024	up.
2025	
2026	## What makes it hard, on purpose
2027	
2028	The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
2029	that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
2030	"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
2031	every page as adversarial and verify what you read.
2032	
2033	## Tips
2034	
2035	- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
2036	- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
2037	- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
2038	- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
2039	- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
2040	  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
2041	- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
2042	- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
2043	  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
2044	  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
2045	- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
2046	  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
2047	- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
2048	
2049	## Starter kit
2050	
2051	[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
2052	submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
2053	Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.
2054	
2055	---
2056	
2057	Source: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md
